newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open flat, eye on second liners.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open flat, eye on second liners.

text.p: Singapore shares opened flat at on Wednesday with continued retail interest seen in low-priced, second liner stocks, dealers said.
At 0230 GMT, after 90 minutes of trade, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was barely changed at 2,215.52 after opening at 2,217.11.

Electronic counter, SM Summit, again led the actives with more than 6.6 million shares traded on syndicate play and rumours that it was a takeover target. Company officials denied the rumours. The shares were at Singapore $0.705, off S$0.01.
Total market turnover was moderate around 50 million shares with losers outpacing gainers by 111 to 95.
Labroy Marine was also among the actives, with more than 3.5 million shares traded. The shares were up S$0.03 at S$1.52.
"There is no fundamental reason for Labroy's activity," said a dealer. "It's just pure speculation and retail investors are looking for cheap, second-liner stocks."
City Development rose S$0.20 to S$12.50 while OUB Foreign led losers, shedding S$0.20 to S$11.00.
